reasoning: Round 70 is a clear repeat of the same compound failure: kelvin_ok=false, gates_pass=false, SENSEC1 both HI and LO unconnected, SENSEC2_HI unconnected. The compiler again produced exclusively non-Kelvin stubs (/CAN_H, /I2C_SCL, /I2C_SDA) and ALL 7 stubs were absorbed or spur-trimmed (absorbed=3, trimmed_spurs=4, removed_orphans=0 → 7/7 total absorption). This fires the compound trigger for Rules 33 (compiler_kelvin_omission), 34 (total-stub-absorption + mandatory_kelvin_bypass), and 35 (M_actual=2, exclusively non-Kelvin/non-diffpair compiler nets → congestion diagnostic + keepout). Those rules are in place and should be force-injecting Kelvin stubs each round. The persistence at round 70 — three Kelvin ratline failures despite 50 standing rules including the full force-injection battery — indicates the constraint is no longer a compiler-priority problem but a physical routing problem: FR cannot find a legal route for cable 1's Kelvin pair regardless of stub injection, likely because track/via congestion in the cable 1 shunt bounding box is blocking the inner-edge escape path. The scorer issue: at the current weights, DRC contributes 30×75=2250 and unconnected contributes 4×450=1800 to the objective, while kelvin_unrouted contributes only 1×1000=1000 — less than DRC alone. This allows FR to settle into solutions that trade Kelvin correctness for DRC improvements, reducing the optimizer's pressure to hold the Kelvin constraint. Raising kelvin_unrouted to 2000 makes a single unrouted Kelvin pair worth more than DRC+unconnected combined at this round's levels, forcing the optimizer to treat Kelvin as the primary axis. The new manager rule addresses the gap none of the 50 existing rules close: there is no ceiling on consecutive rounds in which force-injection is active but the Kelvin pair remains unrouted. Without such a ceiling the loop can run indefinitely on a physically blocked cable, burning budget with no convergence signal. A streak counter per cable that halts dispatch and escalates after 5 force-injection-active but Kelvin-still-failing rounds provides the needed termination condition.

scorer_penalty.rationale: At the current weight of 1000, a single unrouted Kelvin pair contributes less to the objective than DRC violations alone (30×75=2250) at this round's DRC count. This creates an objective landscape where FR candidates are rewarded for trading away Kelvin correctness in exchange for DRC improvement. Raising to 2000 ensures kelvin_unrouted dominates the objective for any round with at least one unrouted pair, regardless of DRC count, so the optimizer has no pathway to an 'acceptable' solution that leaves a Kelvin pair unrouted.

manager_rule: Maintain a persistent per-cable-index integer mapping 'kelvin_force_injection_active_streak'. For each cable index N: increment kelvin_force_injection_active_streak[N] by 1 each round in which ALL of the following are true: (a) compiler_kelvin_omission fired (Rule 33) and force-injected stubs for /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO were dispatched to FR; (b) the subsequent round's failing_reasons still lists /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO with 'has unconnected ratlines'. Reset kelvin_force_injection_active_streak[N] to 0 only when cable N no longer appears in failing_reasons with unconnected ratlines. When kelvin_force_injection_active_streak[N] reaches 5 for any cable N: (1) log 'kelvin_force_injection_ceiling' with fields: (a) round number, (b) cable index N, (c) streak count=5, (d) the per-round DRC, unconnected, and kelvin_unrouted values across the streak rounds, (e) the Rule-35 or Rule-36 congestion keepout geometry that was or was not added during the streak; (2) immediately halt FR dispatch; (3) escalate to human review with the diagnosis: 'Cable N Kelvin pair is physically unroutable with the current force-injection and congestion-keepout approach — the shunt inner-edge escape channel is likely permanently blocked by FR's prior routing; a board-level geometric intervention is required (e.g., shunt rotation, connector repositioning, or a dedicated via-reserved channel for /SENSEC{N}_HI and /SENSEC{N}_LO before FR dispatch).' Do not resume FR dispatch for any round until human confirms an explicit routing strategy change for cable N. This rule is additive to Rules 33, 34, 35, and 36 and does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate; it provides the termination ceiling missing from the current force-injection battery.
